placements.title: Orchard work is timed to the state of the living material and what trial rows show, not to the calendar habit
placements.frame: What does this say about the state of the rootstock or plant material and what a trial showed, and how does that move the date of the orchard work?
placements.why: The position moves grafting from late March to the second half of February. Its grounds are that the rootstock is still dormant and that last year's February trial row took at twice the March rate. Future orchard timing decisions can keep adding to the subject of timing set by material state and trial evidence. The single take-rate figure is evidence held by the position, not a leaf of its own. No existing leaf covers orchard work, and the two existing leaves are about diagnostics and participant data.

mints.name: OrchardGraftingSchedule
mints.title: When the orchard's rootstock is grafted, and the evidence that sets the date
mints.why: The orchard grafting timing is a subject of its own. The 1 October call set the date and this document revises it, so later statements are likely to keep returning to it. No existing stratum holds it.

connections.why: The leaf is about orchard grafting timing grounded in rootstock state and trial evidence.
The position carries the move of grafting to February and its grounds.
